To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

1) the institutional environment of an emerging economy influences how firms learn from their internationalization experiences; and 2) second-hand experience, especially from foreign multinationals, is a key source of learning for Indonesian manufacturers.

the development of AC is influenced by the institutional environment and that the nature of the institutional environment determines which type of experience is more relevant for the development of internationalization-related absorptive capacity.
Indonesian exporters’ absorptive capacity for international markets is driven by both first-hand and second-hand experience.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the role of institutions in influencing firms’ internationalization learning and AC.
the development of AC in the context of a challenging institutional environment, and how firms from emerging markets can learn about internationalizing.
how firms from emerging market economies learn from experience and how this is influenced by their institutional environment.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the development of internationalization-related absorptive capacity is shaped by the institutional context of the firm’s domestic market.
the institutional environment is an important moderator of the development of internationalization-related absorptive capacity in emerging market firms.
institutional environment is important in determining how Indonesian firms develop their absorptive capacity.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the Indonesian manufacturers’ AC development is influenced by both the domestic institutional context and their own strategic decisions, and that these two factors interact to shape their internationalizing learning.

the Indonesian manufacturing exporters have been able to develop their internationalization capabilities by leveraging the opportunities and overcoming the constraints of the institutional environment.
the institutional environment of an emerging market can influence the development of AC, and the influence varies across different dimensions of AC.
The main takeaway from our work is that
, in the context of emerging economies, firms may not be able to develop AC through their own experience, and instead may need to rely on second-hand experiences from other firms.
firms from emerging markets can learn from the international experience of others.
the institutional environment in which a firm operates can influence how the firm learns about internationalizing.
